module.purpose: Provides React Flight client-side module resolution and loading config for Node bundler environments, mapping server consumer manifest metadata to client references and dynamic imports.
module.summary: This module implements the client reference resolution and module loading contract for React Server Components in a Node.js bundler setup. It exposes functions to prepare module destinations, resolve client and server references from a bundler config or manifest, preload modules via dynamic import with async/CJS interop, and synchronously require already-loaded modules. A module-level cache prevents duplicate imports. It is part of the React Flight unbundled runtime and assumes preload is called before require.
module.businessContext: React Server Components rely on resolving and loading client references during SSR. Failure here breaks rendering or hydration of client components in Node bundler pipelines.
classes: ServerConsumerModuleMap (~L29-33): Map from client module IDs to exported client reference objects.
ClientReference<T> (~L42-46): Opaque type describing a client module specifier and export name.
ClientReferenceMetadata (~L39): Opaque alias for ImportMetadata used to unwrap client references.
functions: prepareDestinationForModule (~L54-60): Delegates chunk preparation to ReactFlightClientConfig helper.
resolveClientReference (~L62-90): Maps manifest metadata to client reference using bundler config.
resolveServerReference (~L92-100): Parses server reference ID string into specifier and name.
preloadModule (~L104-141): Dynamically imports module, caches thenable, handles async CJS interop.
requireModule (~L143-167): Synchronously returns exported value from previously preloaded module.
getModuleDebugInfo (~L169-172): Returns null as no debug info emitted on server side.

detail.signature: export function resolveClientReference<T>(bundlerConfig: ServerConsumerModuleMap, metadata: ClientReferenceMetadata): ClientReference<T>
preconditions: bundlerConfig is a ServerConsumerModuleMap keyed by module ID
metadata is a ClientReferenceMetadata tuple with ID and NAME indices

units.name: resolveServerReference

detail.name: resolveServerReference
detail.signature: export function resolveServerReference<T>(bundlerConfig: ServerManifest, id: ServerReferenceId): ClientReference<T>
preconditions: id is a string (ServerReferenceId) expected to contain a '#' delimiter separating specifier and export name
postconditions: Returns an object { specifier, name } where specifier is the substring before the last '#' and name is the substring after the last '#'
edgeCases: If id contains no '#', idx = -1, specifier = id.slice(0, -1) (drops last character), name = id (full string)
If id contains multiple '#', split occurs at the last occurrence
If id ends with '#', name is empty string
If id starts with '#', specifier is empty string
detail.summary: Splits a server reference id of the form 'specifier#name' at the last '#' and returns a client reference object containing the specifier and name substrings.

specLiterals.role: delimiter separating specifier and name in ServerReferenceId

units.name: preloadModule

detail.name: preloadModule
detail.signature: export function preloadModule<T>(metadata: ClientReference<T>): null | Thenable<any>
preconditions: metadata is an object with a specifier property used as cache key
metadata.async is a boolean indicating whether the module is an async CJS module
postconditions: If a fulfilled promise for metadata.specifier exists in asyncModuleCache, returns null
If a non-fulfilled promise exists, returns that promise
Otherwise calls import(metadata.specifier), caches the promise in asyncModuleCache, attaches settlement handlers that assign status/value or status/reason, and returns the promise
invariants: Returned thenable objects gain a status property of 'fulfilled' or 'rejected' after settlement
edgeCases: existingPromise exists but status not 'fulfilled' (pending or rejected) -> returns existingPromise
metadata.async === true -> modulePromise resolves to the default export of the imported module
metadata.async === false -> modulePromise resolves to the module namespace object
stateMutations: asyncModuleCache.set(metadata.specifier, modulePromise) when no existing cache entry
modulePromise.status and modulePromise.value assigned on fulfillment
modulePromise.status and modulePromise.reason assigned on rejection
detail.summary: Given a client reference metadata, ensures the module is imported and cached, returning either the cached thenable (or null if already fulfilled) so callers can await module readiness without duplicate imports.

specLiterals.role: property accessed on async CJS module to get exports

specTests.then: import('mod') is invoked, the resulting promise is cached and returned, and the promise has no status property before settlement
the returned promise resolves to the .default property of the imported module

detail.name: requireModule
preconditions: preloadModule must have been called for metadata.specifier so asyncModuleCache holds a promise
promise.status must be 'fulfilled' or the promise must carry a reason if not fulfilled
postconditions: If metadata.name === '*', returns the entire moduleExports object
If metadata.name is a non-empty string present on moduleExports, returns that property
If metadata.name is not present and not '*' or '', returns undefined
edgeCases: metadata.name === '*': returns whole module exports as-is
metadata.name not found on moduleExports: returns undefined

raises: throws promise.reason when promise.status is not 'fulfilled'
